title: Components of a time series: trend, seasonality, cycle and noise

videos.script: This is every day of Panela's orders for three years. Panela sells meal kits, and every point on this line is one day. {{line}} Ask somebody what it shows and they will say it goes up. That is true, and it is a quarter of the answer. {{up}} Look closer and it is thick, because Mondays are busier than Saturdays, every week, for three years. {{thick}} Each January it sags and each December it climbs. {{year}} And under all of that, every day is a little higher or lower than any pattern would say. {{noise}} A time series is several movements added together. A trend, a season, sometimes a cycle, and noise. Every technique in the first six lessons starts by pulling them apart. {{four}} This lesson names the four, shows each one in Panela's numbers, and sets up the computer you will analyse them on. By the end you will have the data on your own machine and a first program that reads it. {{end}}
